title: Why Do Octopuses Have 3 Hearts? 🐙 #Shorts
description:
Octopuses have three hearts: one big systemic heart pumps oxygen-rich blood through the body, while two smaller branchial hearts push blood through the gills. Their copper-based blue blood (haemocyanin) is far less efficient than our hemoglobin at carrying oxygen, so three hearts keep the pressure high enough to power eight arms and a big brain. But when an octopus swims, its main heart stops beating — so it crawls along the sea floor instead.
